hexagrams.judgmentGuidance: Worth doing: state the rules clearly, keep to them over time, and set the example from your own role first. Avoid: demanding compliance only from the people closest to you, or letting mood take the place of a household boundary.

hexagrams.name: Kuí · Divergence
hexagrams.originalJudgment: Kui: Good fortune in small matters.
hexagrams.ancientContext: The Tuan commentary notes fire moving upward and the lake moving downward, two who share a dwelling and do not share a direction, which is why only small matters go well. It then adds that heaven and earth diverge yet their work is the same, man and woman diverge yet their wills connect, all things diverge yet their kinds correspond, so divergence has a great use. The Xiang commentary teaches sameness that leaves room for difference.
hexagrams.plainLanguage: Dui below, Li above: fire rising, the lake sinking, two forces travelling away from each other, the image of disagreement and mutual mistrust. The judgement grants good fortune only in small matters, which tells you this is not a time for large undertakings and that a narrow scope goes more smoothly. The lines run from a lost horse that returns of itself and a meeting in a back lane, through a cart dragged back and an injury suffered, to finding a true ally in isolation, and finally from suspicion into a marriage proposal. The message is that divergence usually starts as misunderstanding, and once seen clearly, is rarely hostility.
hexagrams.trendReason: The judgment limits good fortune to small matters, discouraging large undertakings. The third six's dragged wagon, restrained ox, and punished driver show hardship; the top nine first mistakes a suitor for a robber, reflecting repeated misunderstanding. Yet the first's vanished regret, the second's no blame, the fifth's blameless proceeding, and the top's fortune upon meeting rain all leave room to turn. The commentary also affirms Opposition's timely use. Overall this is a neutral situation in which measured action is possible. This is the app's interpretation of the text, not a guarantee of outcomes.
hexagrams.coreMessage: Hold what is shared and leave room for the difference.

lines.original: Nine at the beginning: Regret vanishes. Do not chase the lost horse; it returns by itself. Seeing an unpleasant person brings no blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that meeting the person you dislike is a way of avoiding fault. The lost horse need not be chased, because it comes back of itself, and the estrangement is kept from deepening.
lines.plainLanguage: Regret dissolves. The horse that wandered off does not need chasing; it returns on its own. Even someone you dislike is worth seeing, and there is no fault in it. The point is neither to force things nor to close the door.
lines.lifeTranslation: When someone has drifted away, you do not have to rush to win them back; time often brings them round. And keeping basic contact with people you do not click with stops a small coolness becoming a real problem.
lines.reflectionPrompt: That person you would rather not see, is it really hostility, or just a mismatch?

lines.original: Nine in the second place: Meeting the master in a narrow lane. No blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that meeting the lord in a back lane has not departed from the way. It is an informal encounter, and in a time of divergence the value lies in being able to meet and connect at all.
lines.plainLanguage: You meet the person you needed to meet in a side street, and there is no fault. The commentary's phrase about not departing from the way means that informal, private conversation is not a breach of manners in a time of division. It is useful.
lines.lifeTranslation: What will not move in a formal meeting often loosens over a coffee. Changing the channel does not mean you are going behind anyone's back.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is there a lighter setting where this stuck conversation could happen?

lines.original: Six in the third place: Seeing a wagon dragged, its ox restrained, its driver branded on the forehead and nose cut off. No beginning, but an ending.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary attributes the dragged cart to an unsuitable position, and says that a bad beginning with a good end comes from later meeting someone firm. The cart is held back, the ox is pulled aside, and the person suffers injury.
lines.plainLanguage: The cart is held back, the ox is dragged sideways, and the person is hurt. The start could hardly be rougher, yet the matter still comes to a result. The commentary puts the turn down to meeting someone firm, that is, finding the person who can support you.
lines.lifeTranslation: Getting blocked at every step early on, and taking some unfairness with it, does not mean the thing cannot be done. Hold through this stretch and find the right partner, and it often turns around.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is the resistance telling you the thing is wrong, or that your position is wrong?

lines.original: Nine in the fourth place: Isolated in opposition, meeting a worthy man, exchanging trust. Danger, but no blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that meeting in sincerity and incurring no fault means the will can be carried out. Isolated by divergence, one meets an upright and good person.
lines.plainLanguage: In the middle of isolation you meet a straight and honest ally, and the two of you deal with each other in good faith, so despite the danger there is no fault. The answer to isolation is not compromise but finding the right person.
lines.lifeTranslation: When a different position has left you isolated, do not force yourself to blend in. Find one or two people who genuinely understand you, and the work starts moving again.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Who around you actually understands what you are holding out for?

lines.original: Six in the fifth place: Regret vanishes. One's kin bites through soft flesh. What blame in proceeding?
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that when the kin bite through the soft flesh, going forward brings cause for celebration. Biting soft flesh is the figure for coming together with almost no resistance.
lines.plainLanguage: Regret dissolves, and joining with your own kin is as easy as biting through tender meat, so what fault could there be in going ahead? The divergence eases here, and work with people already on your side runs smoothly.
lines.lifeTranslation: Start with the people whose position is closest to yours, where the resistance is lowest. Once that part is done, dealing with the harder side becomes far easier.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Have you been spending your effort on the hardest person to convince?

lines.original: Nine at the top: Isolated in opposition, seeing a mud-covered pig, a wagon full of ghosts. First drawing the bow, then releasing it. Not a robber, but a suitor. Meeting rain on the way brings good fortune.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says the good fortune of meeting the rain lies in all the doubts dissolving. The mud-covered pig and the cartload of ghosts are apparitions produced by suspicion; the bow is drawn and then lowered, and the arrivals turn out to be suitors rather than bandits.
lines.plainLanguage: Isolation reaches its extreme and everything starts to look like a threat: a pig caked in mud, a cart loaded with ghosts. You draw the bow, then lower it, and find these are not raiders but a marriage party. The commentary is explicit that what actually dissolves is your own suspicion.
lines.lifeTranslation: When it feels like everyone is against you, check whether that is fact or invention. Ask the question out loud, and most of the time you find there was no ill will at all.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Are you certain the other side is hostile, or have you simply not asked?

topicRules.career: You are in a phase of divided opinion, so push small, testable items first and hold back the large ones that need everyone to agree. Private conversation dissolves misunderstanding better than a formal showdown.
topicRules.study: You will run into sources that contradict each other, so set the differences side by side rather than rushing to judge. Get the shared fundamentals down before tackling the disputed details.
topicRules.romance: It is easy to guess at the other person's motives and magnify them, so put the doubt into words directly. Differences do not have to be resolved into agreement; keeping room for each other inside what you share lasts longer.
topicRules.family: The gap in outlook is obvious, so avoid arguing face to face in formal settings and let ordinary daily contact soften it. You do not need everyone to think alike; staying in touch keeps the room to turn things around.
topicRules.relations: Hold to sameness that allows difference, and keep basic contact with people you do not click with. A connection that has lapsed need not be chased, since time often restores it on its own.
topicRules.finance: Information is contradictory and there is a lot of noise, so favour small and reversible arrangements and avoid major changes now. This is a general principle rather than investment advice; decide according to your own circumstances and consult a qualified professional.
topicRules.wellness: Doubt and a feeling of isolation build up easily, so talk to one or two people who understand you and cut down the amount of guessing you do alone. This offers no diagnosis or treatment; see a doctor if you are unwell.
topicRules.general: Look for what connects inside the divergence: small matters can move, large ones should wait. Watch how suspicion writes its own story, because asking the question outright usually resolves most of it.

hexagrams.judgmentGuidance: Worth doing: find the common ground first, then break the difference into smaller pieces and check that you each understand the other. Avoid: rushing to prove the other side wrong, or reading a temporary mismatch as opposition.

hexagrams.name: Jiǎn · Obstruction
hexagrams.originalJudgment: Jian: The southwest is beneficial; the northeast unfavorable. It is beneficial to meet a great person. Steadfastness brings good fortune.
hexagrams.ancientContext: The Tuan commentary glosses Jian as difficulty, with danger lying ahead, and calls the ability to halt at the sight of danger wisdom. Going in the favourable direction finds the centre; the unfavourable one runs the way out. Seeing the great person makes the going effective. The Xiang image is water on the mountain, with the noble person turning back on themselves to cultivate their character.
hexagrams.plainLanguage: Gen below, Kan above: water on top of the mountain, hard going, the image of danger ahead and every step laboured. The judgement distinguishes directions and stresses that seeing the right person and holding correct is what goes well. Almost every line pairs going forward into difficulty with coming back to praise, to one's place, to alliance, to friends arriving, to something substantial. Advancing is blocked at every turn, while turning back, halting and gathering allies all yield something. The commentary's phrase about halting at the sight of danger is the key to the whole hexagram. Stopping here is judgement, not timidity.
hexagrams.trendReason: The name means difficulty, and the Judgment explicitly places danger ahead. Five lines describe obstruction in going forward, establishing a difficult tone. Yet the judgment's beneficial meeting with a great person and steadfast good fortune, the top six's substantial gain in returning, and the fifth nine's arriving friends offer openings. It is not the worst state: feasible paths remain amid hardship. This is the app's interpretation of the text, not a guarantee of outcomes.
hexagrams.coreMessage: Halt at the sight of danger and turn the effort inward.

lines.original: Six at the beginning: Going brings obstruction; returning brings praise.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that going forward into difficulty and coming back to praise means this is a time to wait. The moment has not arrived, so nothing should be forced.
lines.plainLanguage: Going forward runs you into hardship; coming back earns you respect instead. The commentary offers a two-word instruction here, which is to wait. At this stage, waiting is the best thing you can do.
lines.lifeTranslation: Stopping as soon as you can see the road is bad is not cowardice, it is judgement. Use the time to get properly prepared; that is worth more than forcing your way through.
lines.reflectionPrompt: The thing you are rushing, is there a real reason it has to be now?

lines.original: Six in the second place: The king's servant faces difficulty upon difficulty, not for personal reasons.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says the minister who goes again and again into difficulty will in the end be free of blame, because the hardship is undertaken out of duty rather than self-interest. The base text keeps the older form of the negative.
lines.plainLanguage: As someone holding a charge, you keep moving through hardship, and not for your own sake. This line gives no verdict, but the commentary says there is finally nothing to reproach: difficulty undertaken as a duty stands up.
lines.lifeTranslation: Some difficulties come with the role. They cannot be dodged and should not be. As long as you are not taking the risk for your own vanity, the hard work stands on solid ground even when it costs you.
lines.reflectionPrompt: The burden you are carrying now, is it for the responsibility or to prove something?

lines.original: Nine in the third place: Going brings obstruction; coming means return.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that going into difficulty and coming back is welcomed by those within, so returning is the fitting choice. Forward is hardship; back is the place where you belong.
lines.plainLanguage: Forward is difficulty; coming back is returning to your place. The commentary says that those inside are glad of it, which means that when you come back the people already around you are pleased. This was your position all along.
lines.lifeTranslation: When opportunities outside keep hitting walls, go back and look after the base you already have. You usually find the people who support you are still there.
lines.reflectionPrompt: While you are pushing outward, is the ground you started from still being looked after?

lines.original: Six in the fourth place: Going brings obstruction; returning brings connection.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary explains the linking on return by a position that is properly held and substantial, so you are not fighting alone. The word for linking means to join and to combine.
lines.plainLanguage: Going alone is hard; coming back lets you link up with others. The commentary's point about holding a substantial position means the task now is not to charge but to connect people to each other.
lines.lifeTranslation: For something you cannot shift alone, find people in a similar position and form a group first. Until the people are assembled, pushing forward is just expenditure.
lines.reflectionPrompt: How much longer do you intend to carry this on your own?

lines.original: Nine in the fifth place: Great obstruction; friends arrive.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that friends arrive in the midst of the greatest difficulty because of centred measure. Conduct kept within proportion is what brings others along.
lines.plainLanguage: At the hardest point, friends arrive. The commentary makes clear that this help is not a coincidence. It is the return on keeping a sense of proportion in ordinary times.
lines.lifeTranslation: The worst moment is when you find out who turns up. Treating people with consistency and keeping your word day to day is how you bank for this.
lines.reflectionPrompt: If you asked for help right now, would anyone come?

lines.original: Six at the top: Going brings obstruction; returning brings substantial gain and good fortune. It is beneficial to meet a great person.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that coming back to something substantial reflects a will set on the inner ground, and that the favour in seeing the great person lies in following someone worthy. The word rendered as substantial means large and abundant.
lines.plainLanguage: Forward is still hardship, but coming back yields something substantial, which goes well, and it favours seeing the great person. The commentary locates the key in a will turned inward: gather yourself, then draw on someone with real judgement.
lines.lifeTranslation: By the end you find the real gain was in going back and putting the inside in order, and in finding someone experienced to point out the direction.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is there someone near you who has already walked this stretch of road?

topicRules.career: Progress will be visibly blocked, so hold off on expansion and consolidate what you already have. Asking senior people for guidance and combining with allies works better than forcing it alone.
topicRules.study: Progress stalls easily, so stop and check whether the method or the foundation has a hole in it. Working through it with a teacher or classmates gets you unstuck faster than repeating the old approach.
topicRules.romance: Pushing things forward tends to hit a wall now, so slow the pace and look after your own state first. Read the other person's silence as needing time rather than pressing for an answer.
topicRules.family: You may be carrying a weight that nobody outside can see, so say plainly what is hard and let the household share it. You do not have to hold everything up alone, and asking for help is not a failure of duty.
topicRules.relations: This favours tending the trust you already have rather than opening new circles. The people willing to show up during the difficult stretch are worth keeping and repaying over the long run.
topicRules.finance: Resistance is significant, so stay conservative, keep cash and flexibility, and avoid increasing exposure or stretching to cover a gap. This is a general principle rather than investment advice; decide according to your own circumstances and consult a qualified professional.
topicRules.wellness: The load is heavy, so reduce rather than add, schedule enough rest, and take accumulated fatigue seriously. This offers no diagnosis or treatment; see a doctor if you are unwell.
topicRules.general: Halt at the sight of danger and turn back on yourself. Stopping and returning are not defeat; they are judgement. Gather your allies and consult someone who sees clearly, and the road opens again.

hexagrams.judgmentGuidance: Worth doing: stop when you meet the obstruction, go back and fill the gaps in your capability, and look for the right support. Avoid: forcing a road you already know is closed, or treating asking for help as weakness.

hexagrams.name: Xiè · Release
hexagrams.originalJudgment: Xie: The southwest is beneficial. If there is nowhere to go, returning brings good fortune. If there is somewhere to go, early action brings good fortune.
hexagrams.ancientContext: The Tuan commentary describes movement out of danger that escapes the danger, which is release. Going in the favourable direction gains the support of many; returning to the ordinary course finds the centre; acting early makes the going effective. When heaven and earth release, thunder and rain rise, and every fruit and plant splits its husk. The Xiang commentary asks the noble person to pardon faults and be lenient towards offences.
hexagrams.plainLanguage: Kan below, Zhen above: thunder and rain together, the image of a deadlock loosening and tension letting go. The judgement says that with nowhere you must go, returning to the ordinary course goes well, and that if you do have somewhere to go, going early goes well. What matters is using the window while things are still loose. The lines begin with no fault at all, pass through catching three foxes, a lesson about inviting robbers, cutting an attachment loose, the release that makes the wrong people withdraw of themselves, and end with a hawk shot from a high wall. Releasing a difficulty means clearing the interference, letting go of what clings, and striking decisively at the one point that matters.
hexagrams.trendReason: The judgment twice gives good fortune, in returning and acting early. The commentary's thunder, rain, and sprouting plants depict renewed life. The second nine's steadfast good fortune, fifth six's fortune, and top six's nothing unfavorable are positive. Yet the third six warns that possessing what does not fit one's position invites raiders, and early action is a condition, hence the rating: Good rather than the highest. This is the app's interpretation of the text, not a guarantee of outcomes.
hexagrams.coreMessage: The knot is loosening; act early and forgive what is past.

lines.original: Six at the beginning: No blame.
lines.ancientContext: The line is two characters long and gives no verdict of fortune or regret. The Xiang commentary says that at the meeting of firm and yielding there is, by the reasoning of it, no fault, because the release has only just begun and nothing has been undertaken.
lines.plainLanguage: Two words, no fault, the shortest line in the hexagram. The loosening has only started and you have done nothing yet, so there is nothing to have done wrong. Staying quiet is the right response here.
lines.lifeTranslation: In the first few days after a hard stretch ends, there is no need to plan the next move. Let yourself slow down. Doing nothing is perfectly fine.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Now that the pressure has lifted, are you letting yourself rest?

lines.original: Nine in the second place: Catching three foxes in the hunt, obtaining a yellow arrow. Steadfastness brings good fortune.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary attributes the good fortune of correctness here to having obtained the central way. In the hunt three foxes are taken and a yellow arrow is gained; yellow is the colour of the centre and the arrow stands for straightness.
lines.plainLanguage: Three foxes are taken in the hunt and a yellow arrow is gained, and holding correct goes well. The foxes stand for cunning interference and the yellow arrow for being centred and straight. Clear the noise, hold to honesty, and things run.
lines.lifeTranslation: Deal with the few people or commitments that have been splitting your attention, then do the work the most direct way available. The difference in output is immediate.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Which three things could you actually clear off your plate today?

lines.original: Six in the third place: Carrying a burden yet riding in a carriage invites raiders. Persistence brings regret.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary calls carrying a load while riding in a carriage a shameful mismatch, and says that when you bring the soldiers on yourself there is nobody else to blame.
lines.plainLanguage: You are carrying goods on your back and riding in a carriage you have no business being in, so robbers come, and holding to it brings regret. The commentary puts it bluntly: you brought the trouble on yourself.
lines.lifeTranslation: Putting on a display beyond your actual weight the moment things improve tends to attract trouble. Keep your position and your capability in proportion and you make fewer enemies.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Does the posture you are taking match what you can actually back up?

lines.original: Nine in the fourth place: Release your big toe. Friends arrive, and trust follows.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that releasing what is bound at the toe is needed because the position is not yet proper. What clings at the toe is a low attachment, and only after it is cut can friends be met in good faith.
lines.plainLanguage: You release the tie fastened to your toe, and only then can the friends who arrive be met with real sincerity. Some small attachments have to be cut before genuine allies can get in.
lines.lifeTranslation: Let go of the old entanglements you keep saying yes to out of awkwardness. The space that opens is what keeps the people who actually suit you.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Which relationship are you still holding on to purely out of habit?

lines.original: Six in the fifth place: The noble person achieves release. Good fortune; there is proof regarding petty people.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that when the noble person releases, small-minded people withdraw. The release is tested and confirmed by whether those people stay or go.
lines.plainLanguage: The noble person who can undo what binds them goes well, and the sincerity of it shows in how others respond. The commentary is direct: once the release is real, the wrong people take themselves away.
lines.lifeTranslation: When you set your principles firmly and cut what needed cutting, the relationships that depended on your wavering disappear by themselves. You do not have to drive anyone off.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Are the people still around you here for your principles or for your vagueness?

lines.original: Six at the top: The duke shoots a falcon atop a high wall and captures it. Nothing unfavorable.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says the duke shooting the hawk serves to release disorder by removing what is causing harm, which is why nothing works against it. The archery imagery of the original should not be read as instruction for action today.
lines.plainLanguage: The duke shoots the hawk from atop a high wall and takes it, and nothing works against him. The equipment is ready, the position is high, the moment has come. This is a closing action, not the opening of a fight.
lines.lifeTranslation: When the preparation is in place and the timing is right, settle the problem you have deferred longest in one go, instead of letting it become a permanent drain.
lines.reflectionPrompt: That thing you have put off the longest, are the conditions finally in place?

topicRules.career: The deadlock is loosening, so act early and clear out the long-standing distractions first. At the same time, keep your role and your capability in proportion rather than making a show of it just as things improve.
topicRules.study: The parts you were stuck on are ready to break open, so go straight back and make up the work you owe. Remove the environmental distractions first, then practise by the most direct method available.
topicRules.romance: Misunderstanding and tension have a chance to clear, so offer goodwill openly and set down the old accounting. If there is something to say, say it now, because an atmosphere left too long will set again.
topicRules.family: This favours forgiving old wrongs and starting again, redirecting the energy spent on past grievances into how you get along today. A subject everyone has avoided can be raised lightly while the mood is easy.
topicRules.relations: Cut the old ties that drain you and leave the space for people who genuinely suit you. Being a little more forgiving of small lapses gets relationships back on track faster.
topicRules.finance: Pressure has room to ease, so deal with the long-deferred burdens first and return to a normal rhythm, without inflating spending the moment things loosen. This is a general principle rather than investment advice; decide according to your own circumstances and consult a qualified professional.
topicRules.wellness: The tension is starting to release, so give yourself a real stretch of rest before gradually resuming, rather than refilling the calendar the moment you can breathe. This offers no diagnosis or treatment; see a doctor if you are unwell.
topicRules.general: Use the loosening to close things out and restart: clear what needs clearing, cut what needs cutting, forgive what needs forgiving. Act early, and keep your bearing in proportion to what you can carry.

hexagrams.judgmentGuidance: Worth doing: undo the constraints you have confirmed, treat old mistakes leniently, and finish the remaining items quickly. Avoid: relitigating a problem once it has eased, or dragging out the part that just needs closing.

hexagrams.name: Sǔn · Decrease
hexagrams.originalJudgment: Sun: With sincerity, supreme good fortune. No blame; one may remain steadfast, and proceeding is beneficial. What should be used? Two baskets suffice for an offering.
hexagrams.ancientContext: The Tuan commentary reads Decrease as taking from below to add above, and insists that the reduction be honest and well timed: even a sacrifice may be offered with two plain vessels, because the intent matters more than the display. The Xiang image is a marsh at the foot of a mountain, with the noble person curbing anger and blocking excessive desire.
hexagrams.plainLanguage: Gen above, Dui below. The marsh sinks lower while the mountain stands higher, so something is taken from one place to complete another. This is not loss for its own sake but deliberate subtraction of what is surplus. The judgement says that where sincerity is present, decrease can still go very well and carry no fault. The lines run from measuring how much to give, through not forcing a sacrifice at all, to cutting away a fault in yourself, and finally to benefiting others without taking anything from them.
hexagrams.trendReason: The judgment's sincerity, supreme good fortune, no blame, steadfastness, and beneficial proceeding form a comprehensive positive statement. The first nine, fourth six, and top nine have no blame, and the fifth six supreme good fortune. The overall hexagram has no general misfortune verdict, except the second nine's warning limited to rash campaigning. Fortune predominates on the condition that decrease arises from sincerity and restraint, hence the rating: Good rather than the best. This is the app's interpretation of the text, not a guarantee of outcomes.
hexagrams.coreMessage: Cut the surplus so the essential can stand.

lines.original: Nine at the beginning: Finish your affairs and go quickly. No blame. Consider the appropriate decrease.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that finishing your own affair and going quickly to help shows a shared purpose, which is why there is no fault. The phrase about measuring the reduction adds that giving should be weighed.
lines.plainLanguage: Close off what is in your hands, then go quickly to help. There is no fault in this. But the giving is measured, not poured out until you are empty. Willingness is good; the amount is yours to set.
lines.lifeTranslation: When someone needs support, wrap up your own work before you go, and decide in advance how much time and attention you can spare. Help offered that way lasts.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Which of your recent commitments is larger than you can actually carry?

lines.original: Nine in the second place: Steadfast correctness is beneficial. Advancing brings misfortune. Without decreasing, increase them.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary explains that this line favours steadfastness because holding the centre is its purpose. There is no need to diminish yourself; staying in your proper place already contributes.
lines.plainLanguage: Holding correct is favourable and pushing outward in haste is not. You do not have to cut yourself back on purpose. Keeping your position and your measure is itself a contribution.
lines.lifeTranslation: Not every act of cooperation has to cost you something. Doing your own part well and standing on clear ground often helps the team more than adding extra on top.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Have you started treating self-sacrifice as the only way to contribute?

lines.original: Six in the third place: Three people walking lose one; one walking alone gains a friend.
lines.ancientContext: Three walking together lose one; one walking alone finds a companion. The Xiang commentary notes that three breeds suspicion, which is why the number reduces itself.
lines.plainLanguage: Where three travel, one drops away; where one travels, a partner appears. The point is that a bond wants to be single and clear. When numbers grow far enough for suspicion, fewer is better.
lines.lifeTranslation: In collaboration, quality beats quantity. Rather than dragging along a crowd with mismatched aims, simplify the arrangement first; the people who genuinely fit will come to you.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is there a working relationship in your circle that is really one too many?

lines.original: Six in the fourth place: Decrease the affliction, bringing speedy joy. No blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that reducing your affliction is itself a cause for gladness. The faster it is dealt with, the sooner the good follows, and no fault attaches.
lines.plainLanguage: What is cut away here is your own fault, and handling it quickly brings the better result. This is the most constructive subtraction in the hexagram: not giving up a resource, but removing the thing causing the damage.
lines.lifeTranslation: If you already know which habit is dragging your progress, change it early rather than waiting for the problem to grow. Handle it sooner and the improvement arrives sooner.
lines.reflectionPrompt: What is the fault you understand perfectly well and still have not acted on?

lines.original: Six in the fifth place: Someone increases them. Tortoises worth ten pairs of shells cannot oppose it. Supreme good fortune.
lines.ancientContext: Someone brings increase, and even a tortoise shell worth ten strings of cowries cannot contradict the omen. The Xiang commentary attributes the good fortune to support from above. Shell divination and cowrie currency belong to the period, not to present-day practice.
lines.plainLanguage: Unexpected help arrives, and even the weightiest reading agrees with it, so the line reads very well. After a long stretch of honest, moderate conduct, outside support tends to appear on its own.
lines.lifeTranslation: When you have been sincere and have not grasped for more than your share, people often step in to help without being asked. Accept it plainly and remember to return it, rather than questioning the motive.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Who has helped you recently without being asked, and have you answered it properly?

lines.original: Nine at the top: Without decreasing, increase them. No blame; steadfastness brings good fortune. Proceeding is beneficial. Gain servants without a private household.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that benefiting others without diminishing them is a state in which the will extends greatly. Gaining servants beyond a single household describes a following that reaches past one family line.
lines.plainLanguage: You can benefit many without taking from anyone. There is no fault, holding correct reads well, going forward suits, and the support you gather is not limited to your own household. Decrease taken to its end turns into increase.
lines.lifeTranslation: When you can create value without squeezing other people, your scope widens by itself, and the people willing to work with you reach well beyond your original circle.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Did your current result come from pressing others, or from making the whole thing larger?

topicRules.career: This is a time for subtraction: close down side tracks that scatter your attention and concentrate resources on what genuinely matters. Simplifying process and display usually beats adding budget or headcount, as long as you cut the surplus and not the core.
topicRules.study: Reduce your materials and subjects, and prefer fewer topics understood thoroughly. Remove the habit that undermines comprehension, such as studying while distracted; it helps more than extending hours.
topicRules.romance: Sincerity matters more than expense here, and a simple, honest gesture carries further than an elaborate one. If some pattern between you is draining both sides, raise it openly and adjust it early.
topicRules.family: Curb temper and appetite, which is exactly what the Xiang image asks. Review chores and spending together for what is surplus, and give the time you recover back to each other.
topicRules.relations: Keep your circle focused rather than broad. Numbers with mismatched aims breed suspicion, so put your energy into the few relationships that genuinely fit; a smaller circle can hold steadier.
topicRules.finance: Trim unnecessary outgoings, reduce over-extended positions and keep the slack as a buffer. This is not investment advice; check anything specific yourself and weigh what you could afford to lose.
topicRules.wellness: Reduce load rather than adding pressure: fewer late nights, fewer things running at once, and deal with the small complaint you already know about. If something concerns you, consult a qualified professional; this is not medical advice.
topicRules.general: Let go of the surplus with restraint so the more important part can stand. Where the motive is honest and the timing is right, decrease opens things up; the one thing to avoid is cutting away the root along with the excess.

hexagrams.judgmentGuidance: Worth doing: trim secondary spending and process on purpose, and keep what you save for the core. Avoid: sustaining appearances you cannot afford, or cutting so deep that basic quality suffers.

hexagrams.name: Yì · Increase
hexagrams.originalJudgment: Yi: It is beneficial to proceed. It is beneficial to cross the great river.
hexagrams.ancientContext: The Tuan commentary reads Increase as taking from above to add below, so that people are glad without limit and the way shines out. It also says that the way of increase, like decrease, must move with the season. The Xiang image is wind and thunder reinforcing each other, with the noble person moving towards good when they see it and correcting a fault as soon as they find it.
hexagrams.plainLanguage: Xun above, Zhen below. Thunder stirs and wind travels, and each strengthens the other, so the flow of resource runs downward and outward. This is the reverse of Decrease. The judgement favours going forward and favours crossing the great water, which makes it a hexagram for action. The lines move from undertaking a large work, through receiving outside help, spending effort on trouble, carrying a major relocation, and giving from a sincere heart, to a final warning about the person who only takes.
hexagrams.trendReason: The judgment clearly encourages action, while the first nine's supreme good fortune, second six's lasting steadfast good fortune, and fifth nine's unquestioned supreme good fortune are excellent. Yet the top nine alone brings misfortune: no increase, possible attack, and an unsteady heart directly warn those seeking only self-benefit. Favorable signs predominate but end with a caution, hence the rating: Good rather than the best. This is the app's interpretation of the text, not a guarantee of outcomes.
hexagrams.coreMessage: Give downward and outward, and support gathers around you.

lines.original: Nine at the beginning: It is beneficial to undertake great work. Supreme good fortune, no blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that only the highest good fortune makes this free of fault, because someone in a low position is not meant to carry heavy affairs. The scale of the undertaking raises the standard.
lines.plainLanguage: This is the moment to take on a large piece of work, and it reads very well with no fault. But the commentary adds a caution: carrying a big project from a junior position means nothing less than excellent counts as acquitting yourself.
lines.lifeTranslation: When you are given resource and authority for a major project, the chance is rare and the bar has moved up with it. Before committing, make sure you can deliver rather than only wanting the opportunity.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Are you ready for the responsibility that comes with this opening, not just the opening?

lines.original: Six in the second place: Someone increases them. Tortoises worth ten pairs of shells cannot oppose it. Lasting steadfastness brings good fortune. The king offers sacrifice to the Supreme Lord. Good fortune.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary notes that the increase arrives from outside. The king making offering to the highest power reflects the ritual world of the period rather than any present-day instruction.
lines.plainLanguage: Help comes in from outside and even the weightiest reading does not contradict it; lasting correctness reads well. What you are asked to supply is not cleverness but steady sincerity.
lines.lifeTranslation: When outside resource or a helpful person moves towards you, the best response is to keep working the way you already work. A good run is not a reason to loosen your principles.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Which of your standards has quietly slipped now that things are going well?

lines.original: Six in the third place: Increase through misfortune. No blame. With sincerity, walk the middle path and report to the duke with a jade tablet.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that using increase for difficult affairs is something this position already holds. Reporting to the duke with a jade token is a ritual form of the period, not a present-day instruction.
lines.plainLanguage: Resource spent on disaster and hardship carries no fault. What makes it work is sincerity, holding to the centre, and reporting upward with something solid to show. Effort given in a crisis is also a kind of increase.
lines.lifeTranslation: Time spent firefighting and clearing up rarely produces impressive figures. As long as you record it honestly and explain it clearly to the people above you, the effort is not wasted.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Does everyone who should know about this mess actually know about it?

lines.original: Six in the fourth place: Walk the middle path; report to the duke and be followed. It is beneficial to rely on support in moving the capital.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that the duke agrees because the intent is to increase what others have. Moving the capital is an administrative term of the period rather than a present-day instruction.
lines.plainLanguage: You hold to the centre, your report is accepted, and on that basis even a change as large as relocating a capital can proceed. This line is about carrying a big shift once trust has been earned.
lines.lifeTranslation: When your proposal is approved and a large change has to be delivered, standing in the middle and accounting for everyone's needs lands it better than holding one position hard.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Has your plan accounted for the people it disrupts most?

lines.original: Nine in the fifth place: A sincere, benevolent heart. Without asking, supreme good fortune. There is sincere appreciation of my virtue.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says there is no need even to ask about this good fortune, and that others returning kindness for your virtue shows the will fully extended.
lines.plainLanguage: Kindness given from a sincere heart is so clearly favourable that the text says not to bother asking. Others answer your conduct with sincerity of their own. This is the fullest line in the hexagram, and the whole of it rests on a clean motive.
lines.lifeTranslation: What you do genuinely for someone else's sake tends to be answered in kind without any management on your part. Getting the intent right works better than calculating the return.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Was your last act of help given freely, or was it an exchange?

lines.original: Nine at the top: No one increases them; someone may strike them. An inconstant heart. Misfortune.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary reads no one increasing him as partial speech, and the blow as coming from outside. The root of the trouble is a mind that cannot hold steady to what is correct.
lines.plainLanguage: No one adds to him and someone strikes at him, because his heart is partial and cannot stay the course. Taking without ever giving eventually removes the outside support you depended on.
lines.lifeTranslation: If you only ever take, the people around you withdraw one by one, and support can turn into resistance. Read this as a description of the situation, not a prediction.
lines.reflectionPrompt: In your most important relationship, are you giving more lately or taking more?

topicRules.career: Conditions favour pushing forward and expanding, especially when you route resource towards the front line and the team. Give support and authority away as you lead; results tend to flow back, provided you are not just protecting your own record.
topicRules.study: This suits adding to and widening what you know, and teaching material to others as a way of holding it. When you meet a better method, switch to it, and correct an error the moment you find it.
topicRules.romance: Give first and say what you mean; sincerity carries further than technique. Warmth here comes from a steady, consistent heart, and a relationship you only draw from will cool quickly.
topicRules.family: Direct more time and resource towards the members who need it most. Admitting a mistake plainly and putting it right repairs the atmosphere faster than defending your standing.
topicRules.relations: This is a good stretch for widening connections, and goodwill offered first is usually returned. Keep it consistent, though; enthusiasm that appears once and vanishes reads as insincere.
topicRules.finance: The income side looks constructive, which suits putting resource into things with long-term value and holding a consistent strategy rather than revising it after a good run. This is not investment advice; check anything specific yourself and weigh what you could afford to lose.
topicRules.wellness: Add positive inputs such as regular movement and a settled sleep pattern, with continuity mattering more than volume, and be encouraging with yourself. If something concerns you, consult a qualified professional; this is not medical advice.
topicRules.general: Giving and moving outward both suit this time, and sharing from the top down gathers broad support. Increase still has to be timely and sustained; a partial heart or an abandoned effort loses the help you already had.

hexagrams.judgmentGuidance: Worth doing: share resources, adopt the better method when you meet it, and correct a mistake as soon as you see it. Avoid: increasing only your own share, or building a short-term gain on someone else's loss.

hexagrams.name: Guài · Resolute Parting
hexagrams.originalJudgment: Guai: Declare it in the royal court. Call out sincerely. There is danger. Announce it from your own town. Resorting to arms is unfavorable; proceeding is beneficial.
hexagrams.ancientContext: The Tuan commentary glosses Guai as decision, the firm parting from the yielding, and asks for strength that stays agreeable and decisiveness that stays harmonious. Proclaiming it in the royal court and calling out in good faith while knowing the danger is what makes the conduct shine; force is ruled out because relying on arms runs to a dead end. The Xiang image is the marsh risen above heaven, with the noble person extending pay and favour downward rather than hoarding virtue.
hexagrams.plainLanguage: Dui above, Qian below. Five firm lines press upward and only one yielding line remains at the top, so this is the clearing away of a last entrenched problem. Guai means to decide and to cut out. The judgement asks you to state the matter openly, to call out sincerely, and to be clear-eyed about the risk, and it says plainly that force is not favourable. The lines run from a premature advance that cannot win, through hardness worn on the face, an impasse where advice is refused, a measured decision in the centre, and finally a position with no one left to call to.
hexagrams.trendReason: Although the judgment allows beneficial proceeding, it also explicitly warns of danger and against resorting to arms. The first nine's blame in unsuccessful advance, third's misfortune from forcefulness in the cheekbones, fourth's refusal to trust advice, and top's eventual misfortune without an outcry are negative. Only the second's “do not worry” and fifth's blameless middle path offer balance. Misfortune and blame outweigh good fortune, hence the rating: Poor. This is the app's interpretation of the text, not a guarantee of outcomes.
hexagrams.coreMessage: Cut cleanly, but argue in the open instead of forcing it.

lines.original: Nine at the beginning: Strength in the forward toes. Going without prevailing brings blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says bluntly that going forward when you cannot prevail is itself the fault. Strength shown in the front toes is strength shown too early.
lines.plainLanguage: The foremost toe pushes off first, the advance cannot win, and that is where the fault lies. Stepping out ahead from the lowest position with strength still short means you carry the risk alone.
lines.lifeTranslation: Leading a confrontation before you have the capability or the backing rarely holds. Weigh your actual odds before deciding to be the first voice in the room.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Are the odds on this move ones you have assessed, or ones you are hoping for?

lines.original: Nine in the second place: An alert outcry. There are armed threats at night. Do not worry.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary attributes the calm to holding the middle way: even armed trouble at dusk brings no need for worry, because the warning went out and the centre was kept.
lines.plainLanguage: Stay alert and raise the alarm, and even if something does break out in the night there is no need for excessive worry. Holding the centre and preparing in advance stops an incident turning into a disaster.
lines.lifeTranslation: When you sense a risk, warn the people it touches and get ready. If it does arrive you have a response, which is far lighter work than scrambling afterwards.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Have you told the people who need to know about the risk you already sense?

lines.original: Nine in the third place: Strength in the cheekbones brings misfortune. The noble person resolves resolutely, walking alone and meeting rain. Though soaked and resented, no blame.
lines.ancientContext: Hardness shown in the cheekbones brings misfortune, yet the Xiang commentary says the noble person who is resolute and resolute again ends without fault, even when walking alone into rain and drawing resentment for being soaked.
lines.plainLanguage: Hardness worn on the face invites trouble. Yet the genuinely decisive person, walking alone, caught in the rain and grumbled at, still ends without fault. The difference is whether the resolve is inward firmness or outward force.
lines.lifeTranslation: A firm position does not require a hard manner. The decision you have to make can be made quietly, and being misread or criticised for a while does not undermine it if the direction is sound.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Does your resolve show in your face, or in how you actually work?

lines.original: Nine in the fourth place: No skin on the buttocks; walking falters. Leading the sheep makes regret vanish, but hearing advice, one does not believe it.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary blames the hesitant gait on an unsuitable position, and the refusal to believe good counsel on hearing that is not clear. Leading the sheep would let the regret pass, but the advice is not taken.
lines.plainLanguage: Restless where he sits and hesitant where he walks. Going along with things the way one leads a sheep would clear the regret, but he hears the counsel and does not believe it. The problem is not the absence of warning but the inability to take it in.
lines.lifeTranslation: When you are stuck between advancing and retreating, other people's suggestions are usually the way out. Rejecting every piece of advice is normally a sign that you are no longer judging clearly.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Whose advice did you dismiss recently without even considering it?

lines.original: Nine in the fifth place: Resolutely remove the purslane. Walking the middle path brings no blame.
lines.ancientContext: Clearing soft weeds with resolve upon resolve, holding the middle way, brings no fault. The Xiang commentary still adds that the centre is not yet fully bright, so a reservation remains.
lines.plainLanguage: Clear away what is soft and entangling with a decided hand, and holding the middle keeps you free of fault. But the commentary adds that the centre is not yet radiant: the handling is right without being admirable.
lines.lifeTranslation: Deal with what needs clearing through proper channels, so the method stands up to scrutiny. At the same time, accept that this round may not have been elegant, and leave room to review it.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Would the way you handled this hold up if you had to explain it in public?

lines.original: Six at the top: No outcry. Misfortune in the end.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says the misfortune of having no one to call to lies in a position that cannot last. Isolation at the top removes every answering voice.
lines.plainLanguage: There is no call left to make and the ending is unfavourable. Standing alone at the very top with nothing answering is the hexagram's closing warning: the situation can no longer be held.
lines.lifeTranslation: Long before you reach the point where there is nobody to ask for help, repair the relationships and say the things that need saying. Read this as a description of the situation, not a prediction.
lines.reflectionPrompt: If something went wrong today, who could you actually turn to?

topicRules.career: You are at the point of clearing an entrenched problem or handling someone difficult, which calls for open process and early warning rather than a head-on push. Pass the benefit down to your team as well; keeping the credit to yourself drains your support.
topicRules.study: Cut methods that are not working and the habit of putting things off, but do not grind through by punishing yourself. When you are stuck, take in what a teacher or classmate is telling you.
topicRules.romance: A hard manner is what tends to cause the damage here, so say the difficult thing calmly and clearly. If you have decided to end something or set a boundary, explain it properly rather than going silent until there is nothing left to say.
topicRules.family: With a long-running problem, cool the temperature before you talk, and bring it into the open instead of sitting on it. Whoever holds authority should look after the most vulnerable member rather than defending their own position.
topicRules.relations: The risk of conflict runs high, so avoid putting anyone in an embarrassing position in front of others. Give warnings early; once both sides have stopped talking it is very hard to recover.
topicRules.finance: Recognise problems early and cut losses decisively, and watch any position that is over-extended or being held on stubbornly. This is not investment advice; check anything specific yourself and weigh what you could afford to lose.
topicRules.wellness: Pressure and tension may be running high, so watch for irritability and disturbed sleep, and keep someone you can talk to. If something concerns you, consult a qualified professional; this is not medical advice.
topicRules.general: The moment for a decision has arrived, and the method matters more than the resolve: open, reasoned, well signalled and shared is what carries. Force, unilateral action, deaf ears and isolation raise the risk sharply.

hexagrams.judgmentGuidance: Worth doing: state the decision and the reasons publicly, and act firmly while keeping a safety margin. Avoid: settling scores privately, pushing people by force, or staking everything while the risk is still unclear.

hexagrams.name: Gòu · Encountering
hexagrams.originalJudgment: Gou: The woman is strong. Do not take this woman as a wife.
hexagrams.ancientContext: The Tuan commentary glosses Gou as meeting, the yielding encountering the firm. In the marriage image the union is not one to keep, yet from the wider view heaven and earth meeting is what makes all things manifest, and firmness meeting the centred and correct lets the way travel widely; hence the exclamation that the meaning of this moment is great. The Xiang image is wind beneath heaven reaching everywhere, with the ruler issuing commands to the four quarters. The marriage language belongs to the period and should not be read as a judgement on people today.
hexagrams.plainLanguage: Qian above, Xun below. Wind travels under heaven and reaches everywhere, so this is the hexagram of the unplanned encounter. A single yielding line appears at the bottom and begins meeting the five firm lines above it, which is why the judgement uses a marriage figure to counsel against a hasty union. The lines move from a brake fastened on the wheel, through the contrast of a wrapping that holds a fish and one that does not, a hesitant advance that avoids real fault, a melon sheltered under leaves with something dropping from the sky, and a meeting at the horn that brings only a small regret.
hexagrams.trendReason: The judgment explicitly discourages marriage, and the first six's misfortune in proceeding and fourth nine's arising misfortune are negative. Yet the second and top nines have no blame, the fifth's concealed excellence and gift falling from Heaven suggest unexpected gain, and the commentary strongly affirms the significance of this meeting's time. Warnings and opportunities have comparable weight, hence the rating: Neutral. This is the app's interpretation of the text, not a guarantee of outcomes.
hexagrams.coreMessage: In a chance meeting, look closely before you commit.

lines.original: Six at the beginning: Tied to a metal brake. Steadfastness brings good fortune; proceeding brings misfortune. A lean pig strains restlessly.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that fastening the metal brake shows the yielding way being held in check. Going forward meets misfortune, and a lean pig fretting and pacing supplies the image.
lines.plainLanguage: Stop as a metal brake stops a wheel, and holding correct reads well; hurry forward and you meet trouble. What the first stirring needs is restraint rather than movement.
lines.lifeTranslation: With an opportunity or a connection that has only just appeared, hold still and look properly first. Restraint at this stage protects you more than enthusiasm does.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Do you want this new opening because you understand it, or because it is new?

lines.original: Nine in the second place: Fish in the wrapping. No blame. Unfavorable for guests.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that the fish in the wrapping is, in principle, not to be extended to guests: what belongs to a close relation is not for wider distribution.
lines.plainLanguage: There is a fish in the wrapping and no fault in it, but it is not to be shared out to guests. What you hold falls within your own proper sphere; keeping it well is enough, and broadcasting it is neither necessary nor wise.
lines.lifeTranslation: When you have something real in hand, hold it steadily and look after the people directly involved. Spreading it widely at this point tends to create disputes.
lines.reflectionPrompt: How far out does it make sense to share what you are holding?

lines.original: Nine in the third place: No skin on the buttocks; walking falters. Danger, but no great blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary explains the hesitant gait as an advance that has not yet found any pull or support, so there is danger without great fault.
lines.plainLanguage: Uneasy sitting still and hesitant walking forward: the position is hard, but because you have not actually stepped out there is no great fault. Staying where you are is uncomfortable and it is also what protects you now.
lines.lifeTranslation: When you feel stuck between two directions and no one is there to pull you through, pausing is not failure. Forcing the step forward is what turns a small problem into a real loss.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is your hesitation a lack of nerve, or your instinct registering the risk first?

lines.original: Nine in the fourth place: No fish in the wrapping. Misfortune arises.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary attributes the misfortune of the empty wrapping to having grown distant from those below, so the answering base is gone.
lines.plainLanguage: The wrapping is opened and there is no fish, and trouble arises from that. Set against the earlier line, the difference is whether the connection was maintained. The commentary puts the cause in distance from the people below.
lines.lifeTranslation: When support you counted on suddenly is not there, it is usually the result of neglect over time. The repair is to go back and rebuild the relationship, not to look elsewhere for a substitute.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Which once-close relationship have you left untended for too long?

lines.original: Nine in the fifth place: Wrap the melon with willow. Concealed excellence; something falls from Heaven.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary reads the hidden pattern as centred correctness, and the thing falling from the sky as a will that does not abandon what it has been given. The melon is wrapped in leaves of the qi tree.
lines.plainLanguage: Broad leaves shelter the melon beneath, the fine quality stays hidden rather than displayed, and something arrives from above. This is the strongest line in the hexagram, and it turns on quiet correctness rather than visible effort.
lines.lifeTranslation: Keep your capability out of the shop window and protect the people and work that deserve protecting, without pushing for recognition. Trust built this way tends to bring openings when you are not looking.
lines.reflectionPrompt: What care do you put in that you would keep up even if nobody noticed?

lines.original: Nine at the top: Meeting with the horns. Regret, but no blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that meeting at the horn is the regret of being at the top and at the limit; since no one else is to blame, there is still no fault.
lines.plainLanguage: The meeting happens at the highest and hardest point, which brings regret but no fault. Standing high and rigid leaves fewer people to meet. That comes from the position, not from anyone's failing.
lines.lifeTranslation: Past a certain level you find there are fewer people you can speak to openly. That loneliness belongs to the position, and accepting it is more useful than blaming others for keeping their distance.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is your current isolation people leaving, or simply how few stand where you stand?

topicRules.career: Unplanned partnerships or personnel changes can appear, so check the other side's background and terms before you commit. Keep tending the connections you already have; once the base drifts away, what you have built slowly leaks.
topicRules.study: Hold to the schedule you already set and watch a new method or new material for a while before adopting it. Consolidating what you have learned helps more than chasing the next source.
topicRules.romance: Someone attractive on paper may appear, and the judgement counsels against rushing in, so give it time and observation. In an existing relationship, watch for the quiet cooling that comes from neglect.
topicRules.family: Keep the household rhythm steady and filter outside interference or advice before you act on it. Put your energy into daily care; quiet effort works better here than public declarations.
topicRules.relations: New faces are likely, so let acquaintance build in stages and keep an observation period. Do not hand anything important to someone you have just met, and do not let your existing circle go cold.
topicRules.finance: Be conservative with opportunities that appear suddenly: hold the brake first, assess second, and note anything with terms that look unusually generous but an unclear origin. This is not investment advice; check anything specific yourself and weigh what you could afford to lose.
topicRules.wellness: Avoid abrupt changes to your routine or forcing yourself to match someone else's pace, and allow yourself to pause when you feel caught between directions. If something concerns you, consult a qualified professional; this is not medical advice.
topicRules.general: This is a time of encounter, with opportunity and risk arriving together. Those who can stop, look properly and hold their existing connections may gain something unexpected; those who commit in haste or drift from the base tend to run into trouble.

hexagrams.judgmentGuidance: Worth doing: identify what a sudden opportunity actually is, and set limits before you decide how far to engage. Avoid: promising on the strength of novelty, or underestimating how quickly a small problem spreads.

hexagrams.name: Cuì · Gathering
hexagrams.originalJudgment: Cui: Success. The king approaches his temple. It is beneficial to meet a great person. Success. Steadfast correctness is beneficial. Using a great sacrificial animal brings good fortune; proceeding is beneficial.
hexagrams.ancientContext: The Tuan commentary glosses Cui as gathering, made possible by compliance that stays glad, firmness in the centre with a response above and below. The gathering has to be correct before it can succeed, and it follows the mandate of the season; observe what gathers, it says, and you can see the disposition of all things. The Xiang image is the marsh risen above the earth, where too much water threatens to break its banks, so the noble person repairs the weapons and guards against the unforeseen.
hexagrams.plainLanguage: Dui above, Kun below. A marsh lies on the earth and many waters converge, which is the sense of Cui: people, resources and strength collecting in one place. The judgement asks for a sincere centre, a person others will follow, correctness, and a willingness to commit something substantial. The lines move from a wavering heart that scatters and gathers by turns, through being drawn in by a steady hand, a strained attempt from outside, a plainly strong position, a rank held without every heart won, and finally tears at the very top.
hexagrams.trendReason: Two declarations of success, plus a beneficial meeting with a great person, beneficial steadfastness, good fortune in the great offering, and beneficial proceeding form a rare concentration of positive statements. The fourth nine has great good fortune without blame and the second six fortune in being drawn together. Adverse elements concern purpose: the first's unlasting sincerity and disorder, the third's sighing without benefit, and the top's tears. Their Images identify confused purpose, incomplete illumination, and unease above. External conditions are favorable but hearts still need uniting, hence the rating: Rather Good, rather than the best. This is the app's interpretation of the text, not a guarantee of outcomes.
hexagrams.coreMessage: Gather around something correct, and prepare while things are strong.

lines.original: Six at the beginning: Sincerity does not last; disorder, then gathering. Crying out, a handclasp turns it to laughter. Do not worry; proceeding brings no blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says the alternating scatter and gathering comes from a will that is itself disordered, not from external conditions. Sincerity is present but does not last to the end.
lines.plainLanguage: The sincerity is real but does not hold, so as the heart wavers the joining and parting waver with it. Even if calling out brings laughter rather than help, there is no need to dwell on it, and going forward still carries no fault.
lines.lifeTranslation: Joining a group before you have settled your own mind naturally runs hot and cold. Rather than worrying how your hesitation looks, work out how far in you intend to be, then take the next step.
lines.reflectionPrompt: How far into this do you actually intend to commit?

lines.original: Six in the second place: Being drawn together brings good fortune and no blame. With sincerity, a simple spring offering is beneficial.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that being drawn in favourably and without fault comes from a centre that has not changed. The simple yue offering values sincerity over abundant provisions.
lines.plainLanguage: Someone introduces you and draws you into the gathering, and it reads well. As long as your sincerity is intact, even the plainest offering is appropriate: the intent matters, not the display.
lines.lifeTranslation: Being shown in by someone willing to vouch for you is rare, so accept it simply. You do not need expensive gestures or an outsized performance in return; doing the work properly is more convincing.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is someone giving you a lift right now that you have not properly answered?

lines.original: Six in the third place: Gathering with sighs. Nothing beneficial. Going brings no blame, with small regret.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that going forward is free of fault because the attitude towards those above is deferential. The wish to gather does not succeed and only sighing remains.
lines.plainLanguage: You want to join and cannot get in, so only a sigh is left and no advantage is visible. Yet if you are willing to set your pride aside and seek a way upward, there is no fault, only some awkwardness along the way.
lines.lifeTranslation: Getting into a circle from outside usually involves being passed over a few times. Lowering your guard and asking directly costs a little face and works far better than sighing from the sidelines.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Are you protecting your pride at the cost of asking the question?

lines.original: Nine in the fourth place: Great good fortune. No blame.
lines.ancientContext: The line text is extremely short: great good fortune, no fault. The Xiang commentary adds that the position is not the fitting one, meaning that only reaching that level of excellence just avoids fault.
lines.plainLanguage: The plainest line in the hexagram says only that this reads very well and carries no fault. But the commentary warns that because the position itself does not fit, nothing less than excellence quite clears the bar.
lines.lifeTranslation: When the resource or influence in your hands exceeds your formal role, the standard applied to you rises, and eighty per cent can still draw criticism. Rather than resenting it, hold your conduct tighter.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is the standard being applied to you rising because your reach exceeds your title?

lines.original: Nine in the fifth place: Gathering in a position. No blame. Without trust, fundamental and lasting steadfastness makes regret vanish.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that gathering while holding the position shows a will not yet fully radiant, which is to say that having the rank is not the same as having people's trust.
lines.plainLanguage: You hold the proper place within the gathering and for now there is no fault. Some are still unconvinced, so what clears the regret is a long, steady, correct accumulation.
lines.lifeTranslation: Taking on a role that leads people does not hand you their trust with the title. Instead of hurrying to prove yourself, keep doing the right things for long enough that trust grows on its own.
lines.reflectionPrompt: Is there someone you assume respects you who is only going along with you?

lines.original: Six at the top: Sighing, tears and a running nose. No blame.
lines.ancientContext: The Xiang commentary says that the sighing and weeping come from being unsettled at the top: the unease is an accurate reading of the position.
lines.plainLanguage: At the highest point of the gathering there are sighs and tears, because the height is not a settled place. The apprehension is clear-eyed, which is why there is no fault.
lines.lifeTranslation: Feeling lonely and afraid at the top is a normal response. Use the unease as a prompt to shore up your relationships rather than performing an ease you do not feel.
lines.reflectionPrompt: In the most visible position you currently hold, what unsettles you most?

topicRules.career: People, resource and opportunity are converging on you, which suits projects that need many hands. Set out a shared aim and a division of work first, and while momentum is strongest, think ahead about what could go wrong.
topicRules.study: Bring scattered notes, materials and unsolved questions into one place, and consider joining a study group. Collecting more is not the same as learning more, so leave time to digest what you have gathered.
topicRules.romance: Meetings and group activities can create openings, and sincerity carries further than display. If your feelings are still unsettled, decide what you want from a relationship before choosing how far to commit.
topicRules.family: Reunions, ceremonies and shared activity suit this time and can reconnect relatives who have drifted. More people means more opinions, so build agreement before announcing an important decision.
topicRules.relations: Your circle widens and connections thicken, so keep your dealings even-handed and people will come to you. Watch that a clique does not form, and do not force your way into a group that does not suit you.
topicRules.finance: Consolidate scattered accounts, spending and resources into one clear picture, and confirm both the purpose and your own capacity before committing. This is not investment advice; check anything specific yourself and weigh what you could afford to lose.
topicRules.wellness: A denser social calendar drains attention, so protect time alone to recover. If you feel persistently hollow or tired after crowded occasions, take it seriously; consult a qualified professional, as this is not medical advice.
topicRules.general: This is a gathering: conditions favour you and people and resource are converging, so gather around an aim that is sound and prepare for the unforeseen. What gathers quickly can scatter quickly, and whether the hearts are truly aligned is the deciding factor.
